historical_extraction_notes: Registered source alias: https://export.arxiv.org/pdf/2306.16406, version 2306.16406v4.pdf. Artifact URL is https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.16406v4. No published-version substitution or web lookup.

Actual bold theorem headings use CMBX12: Theorem 1 on page17, continuing and ending page18; Theorem 2 on page26, ending with (26) at the top of page27. A Theorem 1 citation on page31 uses CMR12 and is excluded.

Theorem 1 includes a local Delta_v definition with k=1..K, weighted aggregate Delta, full expansion (19), three finite-sample conditions, confidence guarantee (20), ST.1 efficiency expansions for general and dagger estimators, ST.2 consistency, and the final additional DS.0 case Delta=0. Do not split or shorten this statement.

Theorem 1 footnote6 states that the sum of estimated pi over S-prime_1 is nonzero with probability tending to one exponentially. It is retained in the claim source_footnotes field with page17 evidence, separate from statement_original. The inventory handoff must preserve that extra field too.
In (19), the final denominator is n times sum pi_v^a without a hat, unlike the other estimated denominators. Preserve and resolve as a source notation issue rather than silently adding hats.

In the finite-sample condition on t, the sum contains a*b+a+b+n^-1. In (20), it contains a*b+n^-1/2*(a+b)+n^-1, with -sqrt(n) multiplying the fraction. These differences were visually checked. Constants are script C1/C2, and the standard deviation sigma_*,GSC is defined in (10). Review possible zero-variance and bound-uniformity conventions.

Theorem 1 does not assume DS.0 for its entire statement: bias correction by the generally data-dependent Delta remains until the final additional DS.0 clause. Do not import DS.0 into the unrestricted finite-sample or ST conclusions solely because the algorithms were motivated under it.

Theorem 2 allows a common L2 nuisance limit E-infinity different from E-star. Its leading influence function includes the additional term [E_P*(E-infinity(X))-r*]/rho* times (1-A_i-rho*). The E-infinity=E-star efficiency conclusion is a separate final branch.

Theorem 2 remainder uses rho-hat^v in the first term and rho-hat^{-v} in D_Xcon. Its Algorithm1 on page26 defines an in-fold rho-hat^v. Remark6 on page27 states that replacing it with an out-of-fold estimator changes the influence function for inconsistent nuisance estimation. Preserve this apparent source inconsistency.

Section2 page7 defines O=(Z,A), finite A containing0, fully observed Z in all populations, iid samples from P*, and r*=E_P*[ell(Z)|A=0]. Section3 page10 changes the setup to an externally named target Q and allows A not to contain0, with r*=E_Q ell. Do not impose the observed-target positivity condition on this general branch.

Page8 defines rho*=P*(A=0) in (0,1) for the observed-target setup. Footnote2 imposes var_P*(ell(X,Y)|A=0)<infinity throughout; footnote3 explicitly defines 0/0=0. These must be retained before declaring denominator cases unresolved.

Page9 gives index sets including empty [M:N], empirical fold laws P^{n,v}, all functions measurable, Pf=int f dP, Lp norm as (int f(x)^p P(dx))^{1/p} for p in [1,infinity], and centered Lp_0. The written norm lacks absolute values and an infinity-endpoint convention; preserve the source and note the issue rather than correcting it.

Page9 defines asymptotic linearity with IF in L2_0 and describes the efficient influence function as the variance-minimizing regular asymptotically linear one. A full definition of regularity is not supplied there; do not read Supplement S9.1 to expand it.

Page10 decomposes Z into K>=1 components with bar Z_0 empty and target-support notation. DS.0 has a known nonempty S-prime_k, absolute-continuity/dominance of target history by the pooled source history, and conditional equality for Q-a.e. history. DS.0-dagger adds 0 in A and in every S-prime_k; S_k=S-prime_k minus{0} may be empty.

DS.1 on page10 is X independent of A under the preceding one-source convention A={0,1}; it does not require equality of Y|X across populations. That binary convention is necessary for 1-a in D_Xcon and (25). DS.2–DS.4 are neighboring distinct conditions, not automatically Theorem2 assumptions.

Page25 defines E-star(x)=E_P*[ell(X,Y)|X=x,A=0] and D_Xcon(rho,E,r)(x,y,a)=(1-a)/rho*(ell(x,y)-E(x))+E(x)-r for rho in (0,1). Corollaries3/4 are not theorems; their efficiency-bound definition can supply referenced meanings without importing their proof conditions wholesale.

Page26 Section4 Algorithm1 is the concept-shift cross-fit estimator: estimate E outside the fold, estimate rho inside the fold, evaluate the residual-corrected loss and combine fold estimates with |I_v|/n. It is not the identically numbered general algorithm referred to by Theorem1.

General algorithms and nuisance definitions on pages11–15 still need source extraction. ST.1 on page16 has an op(n^-1/2) drift-sum requirement and an op(1) L2 pseudo-loss consistency requirement with separate DS.0 versus DS.0-dagger expressions. ST.2 replaces these rates by op(1) and Op(1), respectively.

Remark3 page17 says nuisance limits need not exist outside relevant target supports; such limits were introduced only to illustrate ST conditions. Do not require existence of every limiting nuisance as an extra theorem hypothesis.
